body.statement: Under \texttt{ass:event-date-transport}, \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, and the disclosed one-direction condition \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, for every growth array with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), the interval \(C_\alpha=[\widehat\tau-R_\alpha,\widehat\tau+R_\alpha]\cap[-2B,2B]\) on the regular branch, and \(C_\alpha=[-2B,2B]\) under every declared bad-sample convention, satisfies \[\liminf\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\Pr_P\{\tau(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid z_0\}\ge1-\alpha,\qquad\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid z_0]\le C R_{\star}^{1/2}.\] The proof must uniformly bound the probability of fewer than two usable blocks, undefined variance denominators, donor-covariance small samples, empty opposite-parity fits, and \(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\), and must include the full-range interval's length on those events. Conversely, every interval with the same uniform conditional coverage has worst-case conditional expected length at least \(cR_{\star}^{1/2}\). The \(N^{-\kappa/2}\) expected-length converse, and hence the four-channel length equivalence, uses the maintained direction. The separated calendar-block construction uses actual local-polynomial weights and the full spectrally clipped \(\widehat\Sigma\), and incurs no multiplicative logarithmic phase.
body.proof_tex:
We first record an elementary interval inequality.  Suppose two observed laws
\(P_0,P_1\), with target values \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), possess a common
subprobability measure \(\nu\) of mass \(\eta\).  If an interval \(I\) has
coverage at least \(1-\alpha-o(1)\) under each law, then
\[
 \nu\{\theta_v\in I\}\ge\eta-\alpha-o(1),\qquad v=0,1.
\]
The union bound within \(\nu\) gives
\[
 \nu\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I\}\ge\eta-2\alpha-o(1).
\]
Consequently, whenever \(\eta>2\alpha\),
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}E_{P_v}[\operatorname{length}(I)]
 \ge |\theta_1-\theta_0|\{\eta-2\alpha-o(1)\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
We apply (1) to three subexperiments.

For the treated-mean channel, use the two sign laws constructed in the proof
of the narrowed \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier}.  Their target separation is
\(4\gamma\{\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\}^{1/2}\).  By choosing \(\gamma\) still
smaller, their total variation distance is less than \(1-2\alpha\).  The
measure with density \(\min(p_0,p_1)\) is then a common subprobability measure
of mass exceeding \(2\alpha\).  Equation (1) yields
\[
 \sup_P E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)\mid z_0]
 \ge c_1\left\{\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}\right\}^{1/2}.
 \tag{2}
\]

For the donor channel, choose the separation constant in
\texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} small enough that its common
subprobability mass exceeds \(2\alpha\).  Applying (1) to that family gives
\[
 \sup_P E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)\mid z_0]
 \ge c_3N^{-\kappa/2}.
 \tag{3}
\]

For the spacing channel,
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies a common
subprobability mass greater than \(2\alpha\) and target separation of order
\(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{\lambda/d}\).  Equation (1) therefore gives
\[
 \sup_P E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)\mid z_0]
 \ge c_5\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
 \tag{4}
\]

It remains only to compare these three bounds with the corrected definition.
For each cohort put \(a_s=n_s^{-1/2}\) and \(b=T^{-\lambda/d}\).  Direct
algebra gives
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =a_s^{2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}b^{d/(2\lambda+d)}
 \le a_s\vee b.
\]
Since \(S\) is fixed and \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\), Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
 \left[\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right]^2
 \le2S\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}+2T^{-2\lambda/d}.
\]
The last term is bounded by a fixed multiple of
\(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\).  Hence the square root of the corrected
\(R_\star\) is, up to constants depending only on fixed class parameters, the
maximum of the right sides of (2)--(4).  Taking the corresponding
subexperiment for the largest entry proves the asserted lower bound.

The omitted upper assertion for \(C_\alpha\) is not a consequence of this
argument.  In particular, boundedness alone does not make a Wald statistic
uniformly asymptotically normal.
body.justification: The retained expected-length converse follows from explicit common-submeasure experiments in every nonredundant rate channel.
body.gap: The frozen Wald interval lacks uniform coverage under rare outcomes and finite local-block information.
body.consumer: A future interval should use concentration or replication-aware variance information rather than relying solely on the centered calendar-block sample variance.
